newsitem.title: UK: Cairn, Shell bid for Bangla blocks.
newsitem.headline: Cairn, Shell bid for Bangla blocks.

text.p: Britain's Cairn Energy said on Tuesday it had submitted joint bid applications with its strategic partner Shell Hydrocarbons Holdings B.V. on Tuesday for a number of new oil blocks in Bangladesh.

The submission of bids consolidates the strategic alliance between Cairn and Shell which decided in April to combine their oil and gas exploration and production activities in Bangladesh and neighbouring areas of India.
Bids for the new blocks have been submitted on a 50:50 basis, with Cairn as exploration operator and Shell as development and production operator.
Shell and Cairn also signed definitive legal agreements governing their strategic alliance in Bangladesh and certain areas of India.

The companies have signed an area of mutual interest (AMI) over Bangladesh, under which either party may acquire initially a 25 percent share of the other party's interest in any upstream, power, gas processing or pipeline projects.
The parties have also signed an AMI over the Assam and Tripura regions in north-east India on a 50:50 basis.
Shell has purchased Holland Sea Search Bangladesh B.V. which was a wholly-owned subsidiary of Cairn for $65 million.

The purchase gives Shell an 18.75 percent interest in the Sangu gasfield and associated field development in Block 16, a 17.5 stake in the Semutang field in Block 15 and a 25 percent interest in the remainder of Block 15.
